subject: POC success criteria & KPIs — Atlas Payments (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Devin Martin <devin@atlaspayments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC success criteria & KPIs — Atlas Payments (post-call recap)

Thanks again for the demo earlier, Devin — appreciate you and Aisha taking the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we can align on a clean POC plan. I summarized the success criteria and KPIs we discussed on the call below. Please confirm that these map to Atlas' priorities or suggest edits.

POC overview (scope)
- Integrate Redwood inference as the inference layer for Atlas' transaction categorization microservice for the POC (user-facing, real traffic sample).
- Target dataset: 250k transactions sampled across payment methods and geos.

Success criteria / KPIs (proposed)
1) Latency: median latency (token-generation end-to-end) < 200 ms for 80% of inference calls; p95 < 500 ms under POC traffic profile.
2) Throughput: sustain ~250 concurrent req/s with 99% success (no OOM/errors) during peak simulation; burst to 500 req/s for short spikes.
3) Cost: average cost/token <= $0.002 (target) based on model/config; provide cost/run estimates for 4-week trial.
4) Quality: classification accuracy >= 90% on labeled holdout set (we'll co-develop 1k labeled samples), with precision/recall breakdown per major category.
5) Reliability & observability: request-level tracing, token-level cost and latency breakdown, and access to audit logs for the POC period.

Evaluation plan / tests
- Week 0 (this week): kickoff, share sample dataset + schema; exchange API keys and networking checklist.
- Week 1: integration + smoke tests with 10k transactions; baseline latency and quality run.
- Weeks 2-3: load testing to validate throughput and p95/p99; tuning (batching/quantization) if needed.
- Week 4: evaluation on labeled holdout for quality metrics + cost analysis; executive recap.

Owners
- Atlas owner: Devin Martin (technical lead) / Aisha Roy (product).
- Redwood owner: Jordan Blake (deal lead), Marissa Cole (solutions engineer), Ethan Park (SRE).

Attachments
- Attachment: Atlas-POC-MAP.xlsx (POC milestones & responsibilities)
- Attachment: redwood-poc-sla-template.docx

Next steps
1) Devin — confirm the KPIs above or reply with edits by EOD Friday.
2) Jordan/Marissa — send onboarding checklist and temporary API keys once we have confirmation.
3) Align on kickoff time next week — propose Tue 4/20 11am PT if that works.

Cheers,
Jordan

Thanks Jordan — this captures the call well. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Latency: the <200 ms median target is ambitious but aligns with our user experience goals. Can we get a short-run baseline (no quantization) so we understand the tradeoffs?
- Throughput: 250 req/s baseline is right. For the spike test, 500 req/s is good.
- Cost: can Redwood provide cost estimates for two model configs (opt for high-quality and high-efficiency) so we can compare?
- Quality: the 90% accuracy target is our preference; we can provide the 1k labeled holdout by next Monday. We care most about precision on the "refund" and "chargeback" categories.

We accept the owners and proposed timeline. Kickoff Tue 4/20 11am PT works for us. Attaching a slightly modified POC MAP (minor role tweaks).

-Devin

Nice — thanks for the quick confirmation, Devin. Per your ask, Marissa put together two model/config cost + perf scenarios and a short baseline plan. See summary below and attached runbook. Full numbers in attached runbook (and linked doc).

Baseline runs we propose
- Config A (quality-first): Redwood-curated LLM (8B) at FP16, minimal quantization. Expected median latency ~180 ms, p95 ~420 ms at modest batch; cost est ~$0.0022/token.
- Config B (efficiency-first): quantized 4-bit variant + dynamic batching. Expected median latency ~140 ms, p95 ~330 ms; cost est ~$0.0014/token.

Plan to validate
- Week 1 smoke: run Config A to gather quality baseline on the labeled set.
- Week 2 load: run Config B stress test for throughput profile.
- Week 3 tuning: iterate (batch size, KV cache settings) to hit latency/throughput targets while tracking cost delta.
- Week 4 evaluation: final quality run; calculate cost per transaction across expected traffic mix.

Can we get the labeled holdout and a sampling script for production-like traffic by EOD Monday (4/19)? That will let Ethan kick off the load harness early in the week. Also confirming the kickoff Tue 4/20 11am PT. I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Jordan

Devin — thanks for the attachment and confirmation. Quick note from the engineering side and a couple of operational asks so we don't hit blockers during the POC: 

Operational checklist (short)
- Networking: please confirm that inbound IP allowlist will permit our staging fleet (I included IPs in the POC MAP).
- Dataset: drop the 1k labeled samples + 10k unlabeled sample archive to the shared GCS bucket (we sent a link in the related links).
- API keys & roles: we will create scoped API keys for the POC that expire after 5 weeks; please provide a technical contact for token rotation.

Evaluation specifics (engineering)
- Latency measurement: we'll report median/p95/p99 request times from the request receipt to token generation completion (end-to-end). Please note that client-side network latency will be separated from server-side processing in the report.
- Throughput harness: Ethan will run the first load test and share Grafana dashboards for throughput, GPU utilization, and queue depth.
- Quality evaluation: Jordan will own coordinating the labeled holdout; Marissa will run the inference quality reports and provide category-level confusion matrices.

I'll attach the POC runbook and our recommended initial batch/kv settings in the calendar invite. Looking forward to kickoff Tue 4/20 11am PT.

-Marissa
